arc: hook question ('which database should you use?') → concept ×6 (relational, document, key-value, graph, time-series, vector — each a numbered whiteboard chapter: title, sketched diagram, 'good for', e.g. boxes) → recap ('then pick one:' need → type)

scenes.title: Whiteboard title question with a sketched database cylinder
scenes.summary: On a white board, handwritten 'which database' / 'should you use?' wipe on at 112px, left-aligned. A rough black database cylinder draws itself stroke by stroke on the right (top ellipse, sides, bottom and two band arcs). Below the title 'it depends on the shape of your data' writes on in grey and ink, and a red pen underline is drawn under 'shape of your data'.
scenes.build: createBoard(ctx) from components/sketch.ts: an orthographic three.js whiteboard where strokes are ribbon meshes with a per-vertex t attribute so a shader reveals/erases them like a pen, with rough.js-style jitter and double passes from seeded rng. Text is real glyph outlines (glyphs.ts HAND/MONO vector fonts, sizes in texts.ts) triangulated and wiped left-to-right. Everything is timed with {at, dur} and auto-erases 18 frames before the end.
scenes.reuse: Use as an explainer cold open: change the TEXTS entries (regenerate texts.ts/glyphs.ts for new strings) and the sketched icon. The cylinder is a reusable 'database' doodle.

scenes.title: Hand-sketched users/orders tables with a red foreign-key arrow
scenes.summary: Chapter header '01 / 06', 'relational', 'rows and columns, linked by keys', with 'types of databases' tagged top-right. Two rough tables draw on: 'users' (id, name, plan / 1 ada pro / 2 bob free) and 'orders' (id, user_id, total / 91 1 $40 / 92 2 $12). The user_id column gets a pink hatch fill, a curved red arrow swoops back under the tables to users.id labelled 'foreign key', then 'good for: money, orders, anything that must add up' and 'e.g.' boxes postgres, mysql, sqlite.
scenes.build: A local table() helper composes sketch.ts primitives: rect for the frame, heavier header line, row/column lines, and per-cell text staggered by row and column. hatch() draws 45° strokes revealed left-to-right; arrow() is a quadratic-bezier shaft with a two-stroke head and `bend` sag. header/goodFor/examples are board composites shared by every chapter.
scenes.reuse: The best reference for drawing any table or schema relationship on a whiteboard: swap cell TextIds and column widths. The hatch-highlight + bent arrow is a reusable 'point at this' annotation.

scenes.title: JSON document in a sketched code box with red annotations
scenes.summary: Chapter '02 / 06', 'document', 'each record is one self-contained blob'. A light grey code box wipes on and is outlined by hand, then a monospace JSON record writes in line by line: name ada, plan pro, tags [admin, beta], address { city: london }. Arrows reach back from the right to the tags line ('no fixed schema' in red) and the address line ('nested, no joins'). Then 'good for: catalogs, profiles, content' and e.g. mongodb, firestore, couchdb.
scenes.build: sketch.ts fill() (marker-sweep rectangle) + rect() + text() per code line with float off; lineEnd() computes each code line's right edge from measured text widths so annotation arrows land precisely.
scenes.reuse: Use whenever a code snippet needs callouts on a whiteboard: swap the mono lines and annotation copy; arrows auto-target line ends.

scenes.title: Key boxes arrowing to values, big red '~1 ms' circled
scenes.summary: Chapter '03 / 06', 'key-value', 'one key in, one value out'. Three rough boxes with mono keys 'session:42', 'cart:ada', 'flag:beta' each get an arrow to their values '{ "user": 7 }', '["mug", "pen"]', 'true'. On the right a big red '~1 ms' writes on and is ringed with a red hand-drawn ellipse, with 'per lookup' under it. Then 'good for: sessions, caches, counters' and e.g. redis, valkey, dynamodb.
scenes.build: Loop of sketch.ts rect + text + arrow per row, staggered 14 frames; ellipse() sized from the measured '~1 ms' text for the circled stat.
scenes.reuse: Good for any mapping/lookup diagram or a circled hero number in a sketch explainer; swap keys/values and the stat.

scenes.title: Sketched node graph; a query walks a 3-hop path in red
scenes.summary: Chapter '04 / 06', 'graph', 'when the relationships are the data'. Five hand-drawn ellipse nodes (ada, bob, cara, dan, eve) appear left to right, then black arrows connect them with a small 'follows' label. A query then retraces ada → bob → dan → eve in thicker red arrows, one hop at a time, and '3 hops, one query' writes on in red. Then 'good for: social, fraud, recommendations' and e.g. neo4j, neptune, memgraph.
scenes.build: Nodes are sketch.ts ellipses sized from their label width; an edge() helper finds the point on each ellipse facing the other node so arrows start/end at the rims; link() draws a bent arrow, re-called with red=true and later `at` to overdraw the query path.
scenes.reuse: Reusable for any network/relationship/path-finding explanation: edit the nodes map and link calls; the red overdraw trick shows a traversal clearly.

scenes.title: Hand-drawn line series with a hatched red 'last hour' window
scenes.summary: Chapter '05 / 06', 'time-series', 'timestamped points, appended forever'. A rough time axis arrow draws on, then a wavy upward line of 22 points draws left to right while dots pop onto it in sequence. A pink-hatched, red-outlined window covers the last six points labelled 'last hour', and 'append-only writes' / 'read back by time range' write on at right. Then 'good for: metrics, iot, prices' and e.g. timescaledb, influxdb, clickhouse.
scenes.build: Points generated from summed sines; one strokes() polyline (double=false) drawn over 42 frames with dot() pops timed proportionally along it; hatch() + rect() for the highlighted range.
scenes.reuse: Use for any sketchy line chart or 'highlight a time range' moment; swap the point generator and labels.

scenes.title: Embedding space: red 'puppy' query finds its nearest neighbours
scenes.summary: Chapter '06 / 06', 'vector', 'find things that mean the same'. A grey box marks an embedding space; dots with words pop in — cat, kitten, lion, dog on the left, car, truck, bus on the right. A red dot labelled '"puppy"' lands, red arrows reach to dog, kitten and cat, and a red ellipse rings the animal cluster. 'nearest neighbours' / 'by meaning, not keywords' write on at right, then 'good for: semantic search, rag, recs' and e.g. pgvector, pinecone, qdrant.
scenes.build: sketch.ts dot + text per word at fixed coordinates; arrows computed from unit vectors so they start/stop just off each dot; ellipse() for the cluster ring.
scenes.reuse: Clear template for explaining embeddings, semantic search, clustering or similarity: swap words/positions and the query. Very legible at a glance.

scenes.title: 'then pick one:' — six needs arrow to six boxed database types
scenes.summary: 'then pick one:' writes on at top-left. Six rows follow, 16 frames apart: a need on the left ('money must add up', 'nested records, shape keeps changing', 'hot lookups by a single key', 'relationships are the query', 'metrics over time', 'search by meaning') with a hand-drawn arrow to a boxed type on the right (relational, document, key-value, graph, time-series, vector). Everything erases at the end.
scenes.build: Loop of sketch.ts text + arrow + labelBox per row with a fixed right-hand column; the chapter tag is placed already-revealed (at:-100) so it carries over from earlier scenes and erases with the board.
scenes.reuse: Simple, reusable recap/decision table for any explainer: swap the six need/type pairs (row count is a loop bound).
